messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] us-east-1 streaming-pipeline.p99 > 1200ms for 6m (SLO breach). Alert ID: ALRT-3890. Paging events observed on inference-nodes-*/nvme. cc @oncall

maya: seeing p95 jump to ~420ms, p99 ~1.3s. Streaming stalls spiking at tail, customers reporting partial responses.

sam: linking traces — looks like a bunch of requests hit KV cache miss then long decode tail. Prefill workers spiking CPU while decode workers sit idle.

raj: any correlation with recent kv-eviction tweak from last deploy? I remember we changed LRU window size yesterday.

jess: yep changed eviction window to 2m to reduce mem pressure. Telemetry shows cache_fragment_ratio=0.71 and active_prefill_workers=120 vs active_decode_workers=32 on shard-7.

chris: that ratio is high. fragmentation + aggressive prefill could be thrashing pages -> kernel paging to NVMe, causing large tail.

maya: quick impact check: about 18 sessions in last 10m had streaming stalls >5s, 2 sessions timed out and returned 500 to customer. Affected model: rdx-3b-qat on shard-7 in us-east-1.

sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable prefill on shard-7 (fast) 2) increase decode worker pool to match prefill (20-30m rolling) 3) revert eviction change (risky) 4) route streaming traffic off shard-7 to warm shard (routing rule update).

raj: let's do safe, fast -> disable prefill on affected shards and scale decode workers. Also add a temporary soft cap on prefill concurrency.

jess: rolling command to disable prefill config on shard-7: ```
# run from ops-control
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN" https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/shards/shard-7/config -d '{"prefill_enabled":false}'
```

chris: I'm applying the curl now. watching metrics.

chris: applied — prefill_enabled=false returned 200. prefill_active_count -> 12 from 120 within 45s.

maya: CPU on prefill nodes dropping, decode queues rising a bit then draining. p95 down to 260ms, p99 trending to 520ms.

sam: good. also bumped decode pool on shard-7: ```
kubectl scale deploy/decode-workers -n inference --replicas=80 -l shard=shard-7
```

sam: replicas scaled to 80. decode workers caught up and KV miss decode latency improved.

jess: paging rates on affected nodes decreased (vmstat shows pgpgin/pgpgout down to baseline). kernel page-faults per sec dropped 6x.

maya: customer impact update: we had 0.04% error spike across all traffic, concentrated in us-east-1. Notifying SRE on-call to prepare for SOC if customers escalate.

incident-bot: Incident declared: INC-3890 - KV cache fragmentation causing prefill/decode imbalance -> streaming tail stalls. Priority: P1. Incident lead assigned: maya.

raj: can we also add a quick traffic split to route streaming to rdx-3b-qat-warm in us-west? Fallback reduces latency and gives time for patch.

chris: updating smart-router policy now: adding a temporary routing rule to divert 30% streaming traffic away from shard-7. Policy change pushed.

maya: confirm metrics after traffic split: p99 global down to ~480ms, us-east-1 p99 ~740ms but trending down. Streaming stall count falls.

sam: root cause hypothesis: eviction window shrink increased micro-fragmentation of KV shards; combined with aggressive prefill concurrency created hot prefill fanout causing working set to exceed contiguous cache segments -> higher page fragmentation and NVMe paging under load. Prefill vs decode imbalance amplified tail when prefill workers competed for IO.

jess: actionable next steps (short term): 1) keep prefill disabled on shard-7, 2) revert eviction window to previous value on a canary set of shards, 3) implement prefill concurrency soft cap and queue backpressure, 4) emergency patch to prefer decode-local prefill affinity.

chris: long term: add fragmentation gauges to KV telemetry, autotune eviction window by measured fragment_ratio, and limit prefill per-shard by decode capacity.

maya: documenting customer impact: affected customers = internal-monitoring, partner-x, and 3 dev accounts. Visible symptoms: streaming stalls, some 500s. No data loss. Response: mitigations applied, watch window 30m, will escalate to incident review if p99 > 600ms persists.

sam: I'm taking incident lead for next hour to drive revert and a controlled canary. @jess please coordinate the revert canary patch and notify infra.

jess: starting canary revert on shard-12 (non-prod) then shard-4 (prod small). revert command: ```
PATCH /api/v1/kv/config {"eviction_window_secs":300}
```

chris: logs show one node with io.wait spike -> isolating node for follow-up (inference-node-7a). Marking for post-incident analysis.

maya: handoff note: sam will run the revert canary and track customer-facing telemetry. I'll stay available for escalation. If p99 > 600ms again -> promote to SEV.

raj: thanks team. tagging for postmortem: kv-service, prefill, router, runtime. Add timeline + config diff to INC-3890 ticket.

sam: will update incident ticket with mitigation commands, metrics, and next steps. Leaving this thread open while monitoring.

chris: monitoring 30m window. current p99 430ms.

jess: can everyone react with :thumbsup: when you ack the handoff and plan?

maya: maya: :thumbsup:

sam: sam: :thumbsup:

raj: raj: :thumbsup:

chris: chris: :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-3890 still open. Next status update scheduled in 15m.
